stages.name: Foundations
stages.goal: Both projects build, test and lint in CI. Neo4j, Redis and Service Bus run in Docker, the graph driver and schema migrations exist, and the Neo4j test harness wipes and round-trips the graph for every test.

stages.name: Domain rules
stages.goal: Every business rule is a pure, tested function (status, freshness, schedules, reply parsing, booking states, criteria filter, registration gate, alerts, templates), and the FHIR-to-graph mapper and resource store round-trip resources through Neo4j.

stages.name: Capacity loop: core and storage
stages.goal: Each port ships with its Neo4j adapter and round-trip tests: services, capacity, bookings, cases, people, criteria, registrations, flags, audit, outbox, unit of work, idempotency, tokens and credentials. Report, confirm, prompt and missed-report use cases run against the real graph; Redis and Service Bus adapters pass their contract tests.

stages.name: Capacity loop: channels, API and wall board
stages.goal: A reporter answers a text or a link and the wall board changes live. Milestone A: the board runs on real data.

stages.name: Advisor call
stages.goal: An advisor captures needs, sees filtered options with data age, records phoned and declined positions and closes the case. The shift lead chases late reporters and sets services up. Milestone B: pilot-ready (the pilot cut line).

stages.name: Booking by text and link
stages.goal: Advisors request bookings; services confirm or decline by text, link or app; timers expire silence; withdrawals and cancellations work.

stages.name: Registration and approval
stages.goal: Services are invited from the scope list, register themselves, and go live only after checks, a call-back, criteria second approval and a test prompt.

stages.name: Reporter app, PIN, push and alerts
stages.goal: Installed web app with PIN and push for reporters; COO and ICB users get chosen alerts with acknowledgement and escalation.

stages.name: Shift lead tools, clinical advice and safety
stages.goal: Suspend, remove, move, flags, audit replay, the clinical advice queue and safety concern reporting.

stages.name: Observability and support console
stages.goal: Browser and backend telemetry without personal values, friction rules, aggregates, and the consent-based support console.

stages.name: Later
stages.goal: Map and travel time, planning view, product tour and training, RDF export, the second SMS provider.

title: StrEnum members from different enums with the same value compare equal, so key lookups by (enum class, value)
body: StrEnum members are str subclasses. ServiceCategory.OTHER == ReferrerType.OTHER is True, and their hashes match, so a dict keyed by member can return the wrong entry across enums. Key per-enum lookups by (type(member), member.value), and take the coding system from type(member), never from the value alone. title: London clock change: local 01:00-01:59 on 2026-03-29 is not monotonic
body: On 2026-03-29, local 01:00-01:59 maps to 02:00-02:59 BST, and local 02:00 maps to the same instant as local 01:00. Wall-clock order is not monotonic across the gap. Schedule builders (D03, D04) must not place a due time inside 01:00-02:00 on that date, and must compare instants, never local times. Use london_time.london_to_utc from F06. Found by F06.

stages.name: Foundations
stages.goal: Both projects build, test and lint in CI. Neo4j, Redis and Service Bus run in Docker, the graph driver and schema migrations exist, and the Neo4j test harness wipes and round-trips the graph for every test.

stages.name: Domain rules
stages.goal: Every business rule is a pure, tested function (status, freshness, schedules, reply parsing, booking states, criteria filter, registration gate, alerts, templates), and the FHIR-to-graph mapper and resource store round-trip resources through Neo4j.

stages.name: Capacity loop: core and storage
stages.goal: Each port ships with its Neo4j adapter and round-trip tests: services, capacity, bookings, cases, people, criteria, registrations, flags, audit, outbox, unit of work, idempotency, tokens and credentials. Report, confirm, prompt and missed-report use cases run against the real graph; Redis and Service Bus adapters pass their contract tests.

stages.name: Capacity loop: channels, API and wall board
stages.goal: A reporter answers a text or a link and the wall board changes live. Milestone A: the board runs on real data.

stages.name: Advisor call
stages.goal: An advisor captures needs, sees filtered options with data age, records phoned and declined positions and closes the case. The shift lead chases late reporters and sets services up. Milestone B: pilot-ready (the pilot cut line).

stages.name: Booking by text and link
stages.goal: Advisors request bookings; services confirm or decline by text, link or app; timers expire silence; withdrawals and cancellations work.

stages.name: Registration and approval
stages.goal: Services are invited from the scope list, register themselves, and go live only after checks, a call-back, criteria second approval and a test prompt.

stages.name: Reporter app, PIN, push and alerts
stages.goal: Installed web app with PIN and push for reporters; COO and ICB users get chosen alerts with acknowledgement and escalation.

stages.name: Shift lead tools, clinical advice and safety
stages.goal: Suspend, remove, move, flags, audit replay, the clinical advice queue and safety concern reporting.

stages.name: Observability and support console
stages.goal: Browser and backend telemetry without personal values, friction rules, aggregates, and the consent-based support console.

stages.name: Later
stages.goal: Map and travel time, planning view, product tour and training, RDF export, the second SMS provider.

title: Service Bus emulator image has no shell, so it cannot run its own healthcheck
body: The emulator image (servicebus-emulator:2.0.1) has no /bin/sh, bash or curl; docker exec and a shell healthcheck both fail. Its /health endpoint on port 5300 returns 200 when ready. F04 uses a probe container (servicebus-ready, the SQL image, which has bash) that polls http://servicebus-emulator:5300/health, so up --wait waits for the emulator. Use the same pattern for any service that ships without a shell. The emulator needs SQL Server 2022 (mssql/server), not Azure SQL Edge, per current MS docs.

title: Duplicate detection on inbound.replies makes a repeat send of the same id fail for 20 seconds
body: Queue inbound.replies has RequiresDuplicateDetection true with DuplicateDetectionHistoryTimeWindow PT20S. The smoke test sends message id smoke-1 each run, so a second run within 20 seconds receives nothing and fails. Wait 20 seconds, or use a unique id in tests that send to inbound.replies (the F10 harness should do this). Documented in infra/README.md.

title: docker compose restart returns before Neo4j accepts connections
body: After docker compose restart neo4j, the container is Up but its healthcheck is still starting, so an immediate cypher-shell or driver call gets connection refused. Run docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait neo4j (or poll health) before connecting. Data does persist across restart; down -v removes it.

stages.name: Foundations
stages.goal: Both projects build, test and lint in CI. Neo4j, Redis and Service Bus run in Docker, the graph driver and schema migrations exist, and the Neo4j test harness wipes and round-trips the graph for every test.

stages.name: Domain rules
stages.goal: Every business rule is a pure, tested function (status, freshness, schedules, reply parsing, booking states, criteria filter, registration gate, alerts, templates), and the FHIR-to-graph mapper and resource store round-trip resources through Neo4j.

stages.name: Capacity loop: core and storage
stages.goal: Each port ships with its Neo4j adapter and round-trip tests: services, capacity, bookings, cases, people, criteria, registrations, flags, audit, outbox, unit of work, idempotency, tokens and credentials. Report, confirm, prompt and missed-report use cases run against the real graph; Redis and Service Bus adapters pass their contract tests.

stages.name: Capacity loop: channels, API and wall board
stages.goal: A reporter answers a text or a link and the wall board changes live. Milestone A: the board runs on real data.

stages.name: Advisor call
stages.goal: An advisor captures needs, sees filtered options with data age, records phoned and declined positions and closes the case. The shift lead chases late reporters and sets services up. Milestone B: pilot-ready (the pilot cut line).

stages.name: Booking by text and link
stages.goal: Advisors request bookings; services confirm or decline by text, link or app; timers expire silence; withdrawals and cancellations work.

stages.name: Registration and approval
stages.goal: Services are invited from the scope list, register themselves, and go live only after checks, a call-back, criteria second approval and a test prompt.

stages.name: Reporter app, PIN, push and alerts
stages.goal: Installed web app with PIN and push for reporters; COO and ICB users get chosen alerts with acknowledgement and escalation.

stages.name: Shift lead tools, clinical advice and safety
stages.goal: Suspend, remove, move, flags, audit replay, the clinical advice queue and safety concern reporting.

stages.name: Observability and support console
stages.goal: Browser and backend telemetry without personal values, friction rules, aggregates, and the consent-based support console.

stages.name: Later
stages.goal: Map and travel time, planning view, product tour and training, RDF export, the second SMS provider.

title: Neo4j rejects a data write in the same transaction as a schema change
body: Running CREATE CONSTRAINT/INDEX and a MERGE in one managed transaction fails with Neo.ClientError.Transaction.ForbiddenDueToTransactionType (Tried to execute Write query after executing Schema modification). Do it instead: run the schema statement in its own execute_write, then the bookkeeping write in a second one. Both must be idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS, MERGE). See backend/src/diucs/adapters/outbound/graph_store/migrations.py.

title: Run an isolated Neo4j beside the shared stack with a port override file
body: Start a second stack without touching diucs-local: docker compose -p diucs-<id> -f infra/docker-compose.yml -f <override.yml> up -d --wait neo4j, where override.yml sets services.neo4j.ports to '!override' with free host ports (for example 17474:7474 and 17687:7687). Point NEO4J_URI at that port. Tear it down with: docker compose -p diucs-<id> -f ... down -v. Never run a wiping test against the default 7687 port.

title: Neo4j tests: the harness owns the container; wipe only through the harness driver
body: F10 starts a throwaway Neo4j per pytest session (docker run, free port, unique name) and sets NEO4J_URI for that session (DEC-013). NEO4J_URI from the shell is ignored by the harness. Three traps found: (1) pytest collection hooks that call add_marker(usefixtures) are too late, because the fixture closure is built at collection; append the name to item.fixturenames instead (pytest-asyncio does the same). (2) A test module that defines its own module-scoped neo4j_driver (test_infra_up.py does, for the compose stack) overrides the name, so clean_graph must depend on harness_driver, not neo4j_driver, or it wipes the wrong instance. (3) Async fixtures cannot call getfixturevalue on another async fixture (nested loop); use a plain fixture dependency. G01 test_driver.py now uses the session neo4j_driver; its module fixture was removed. Use loop_scope session for tests that use the driver.

title: Container holds Neo4jConnection; call startup() before use
body: container.neo4j replaces container.neo4j_driver (G14). Call container.startup() before any use and container.shutdown() on exit. The driver is reachable only through the connection; use connection.session(), run_read or run_write. Tasks affected: P06, I03, I05, I08, R01.

title: In-flight reads fail about 30 s after Neo4j stops, not at once
body: The driver retries managed transactions for about 30 s before a read raises a retryable error (measured in G14). Workers and health checks must budget for that delay and must not treat a 5 s timeout as proof of failure during a restart.

title: Harness container is restartable: use harness_container to stop and start Neo4j in tests
body: The F10 harness container is started without --rm (F11), so it survives docker stop and docker start on the same port with its data. To test recovery, take the session fixture harness_container (a ThrowawayNeo4j) and call stop_container(c), then start_container(c), then wait_until_ready(c) before connecting: docker start returns before Neo4j accepts connections (L7). Always start the container again in a finally block. Do not start your own restartable container; the recovery_neo4j workaround in G14 is gone. harness_driver, harness_container and clean_graph are unchanged. Found by F11.

stages.name: Foundations
stages.goal: Both projects build, test and lint in CI. Neo4j, Redis and Service Bus run in Docker, the graph driver and schema migrations exist, and the Neo4j test harness wipes and round-trips the graph for every test.

stages.name: Domain rules
stages.goal: Every business rule is a pure, tested function (status, freshness, schedules, reply parsing, booking states, criteria filter, registration gate, alerts, templates), and the FHIR-to-graph mapper and resource store round-trip resources through Neo4j.

stages.name: Capacity loop: core and storage
stages.goal: Each port ships with its Neo4j adapter and round-trip tests: services, capacity, bookings, cases, people, criteria, registrations, flags, audit, outbox, unit of work, idempotency, tokens and credentials. Report, confirm, prompt and missed-report use cases run against the real graph; Redis and Service Bus adapters pass their contract tests.

stages.name: Capacity loop: channels, API and wall board
stages.goal: A reporter answers a text or a link and the wall board changes live. Milestone A: the board runs on real data.

stages.name: Advisor call
stages.goal: An advisor captures needs, sees filtered options with data age, records phoned and declined positions and closes the case. The shift lead chases late reporters and sets services up. Milestone B: pilot-ready (the pilot cut line).

stages.name: Booking by text and link
stages.goal: Advisors request bookings; services confirm or decline by text, link or app; timers expire silence; withdrawals and cancellations work.

stages.name: Registration and approval
stages.goal: Services are invited from the scope list, register themselves, and go live only after checks, a call-back, criteria second approval and a test prompt.

stages.name: Reporter app, PIN, push and alerts
stages.goal: Installed web app with PIN and push for reporters; COO and ICB users get chosen alerts with acknowledgement and escalation.

stages.name: Shift lead tools, clinical advice and safety
stages.goal: Suspend, remove, move, flags, audit replay, the clinical advice queue and safety concern reporting.

stages.name: Observability and support console
stages.goal: Browser and backend telemetry without personal values, friction rules, aggregates, and the consent-based support console.

stages.name: Later
stages.goal: Map and travel time, planning view, product tour and training, RDF export, the second SMS provider.

title: Twice-a-day 14:00 follows the rule book, not the prompt's closing exception (DEC-024)
body: domain-rules 1.4 gives 14:00 unless the service opens after 14:00. The D04 prompt also dropped 14:00 when the service closes at or before 14:00, and the first code used a plain start<14:00<end check, which lost 14:00 for overnight windows such as 10:00 to 06:00. title: SMS: a concatenated UCS-2 segment holds 67 units, so 2 segments hold 134, not 137
body: One UCS-2 message holds 70 UTF-16 code units. A concatenated UCS-2 message holds 67 per segment, so 135 characters need three segments. GSM-7 holds 160, then 153 per segment; extension characters count two; any non-GSM character (for example 'ł') makes the whole text UCS-2. Use sms_length.sms_segments, which is tested at the boundaries (134/135, 70/71, 160/161, 306/307). Do not count segments by len().

title: A datetime passes as a date: refuse it in calendar-day rules
body: datetime is a subclass of date, so isinstance(x, date) is True for an aware instant, and comparisons with a date do not give the right day near midnight in London. D21 (criteria_workflow.py, DEC-038) refuses datetime explicitly in is_review_overdue, review_reminder_due and next_review_by. Callers derive the day with london_time.to_london(instant).date() (lesson L4). Use the same guard in any date-only rule: U30, U31 and any reminder or freshness check that takes a day, and test it with a datetime input.

title: Review-by and overdue functions ignore the version status; U31 must read only the current version
body: D21 is_review_overdue and review_reminder_due check dates only, for any criteria version (the prompt states this). A superseded or retired version with a past review-by therefore returns overdue=True. U31 must take the current version per service (CriteriaRepository.current_for_service) before it sets the criteria-overdue flag or sends a reminder, and must not read history. DEC-038 records this; owner to confirm.

title: Pairing codes draw one digit per call: rng(10), six times
body: new_pairing_code (D26, domain/rules/tokens.py) calls the random source six times, each with bound 10, and refuses any result that is not an int from 0 to 9 (bool included). A single call with bound 1000000 does not match the prompt's test (lambda n: 7 gives 777777). New support codes use the same pattern with bound 31 (the alphabet length), eight calls. Callers that inject a random source for a pairing or support code must follow this shape. A ValidationFailed from these functions names only the field, never the code. See DEC-044.

title: Text-code expiry and 30-day re-verification must compare UTC instants (DEC-044)
body: D27 identity_policy.py converts every datetime to UTC before it compares, subtracts or adds a timedelta. Same-zone London datetimes give wall-clock arithmetic, so 10 minutes or 30 days across 2026-10-25 come out an hour wrong. Tests use London-zoned inputs that cross the change (test_expiry_is_judged_on_the_real_instant_across_the_clock_change, test_thirty_days_is_counted_on_the_real_instant_across_the_clock_change). Also: a PIN's fifth wrong try gives outcome locked, a verified code is expired on any later entry, naive datetimes raise ValidationFailed, and a timestamp in the future fails closed. The PIN never enters the module; the caller passes a boolean. Read DEC-044 before U25, U32, P10 or I13.

title: Grouped prompts: group_due returns PromptGroup, letters refuse duplicate names (DEC-048)
body: group_due returns list[PromptGroup] (GroupedItem with service_id, name, due, letter), not the list[list] that contracts.md said; contracts.md is corrected. Items join a group only if less than 10 minutes after the group's first item (anchored, not chained). Letters follow name order and only groups of 2 or more get letters. Duplicate names in one group or in letters_for raise ValidationFailed, and so does a repeated service_id. Due times are converted to UTC before comparing (L52). Consumers (U04, U05, D14, D15 C9/C10) should use PromptGroup.items and each item's letter, and never assume letters exist for a single-service prompt. See DEC-048.

title: The mapper writes no json property; from_graph is the only rebuild path (DEC-001 overrides R1)
body: G02 follows DEC-001, not fhir-data-model.md R1. Nodes have no json property, so tests that compare a node's json with the canonical resource do not apply. Use from_graph(to_graph(r)) == r for round trips, and assert graph safety (no map, no list of maps, no JSON-looking string). to_graph reads elements in sorted order so key order cannot change the fragment. Datetimes stay as the FHIR ISO strings in the fragment; G05 converts them to Neo4j datetime at write and must keep the zone text, because a Neo4j datetime does not keep the offset (DEC-049 item 2, open risk). Unmapped elements raise UnsupportedElement(path); never drop them. Affects G03, G04, G05.

title: Shared Concept and Identifier nodes: G05 must not overwrite them, and fragments need them
body: G03 (DEC-051) stores a Concept node keyed Concept|system|code with display and version on the node, and an Identifier node keyed Identifier|system|value. Two things follow for G04 and G05. (1) Across resources, the same concept can arrive with a different display or version. A MERGE that SETs display or version will overwrite the other resource's value. Write display and version only when the node has none, or refuse a change, and never move them to a relationship silently. Identifier use is on the relationship, not the node: keep it there. (2) from_graph rebuilds codings and identifiers from the Concept and Identifier nodes in the fragment, not from the relationship alone. A reader that loads only the root and its relationships gets NotFound. Load the nodes at the ends of IDENTIFIED_BY, CODE, CATEGORY and every other concept relationship. Lists of CodeableConcept carry conceptOrder: a list of one differs from a single CodeableConcept, so keep the property when writing and reading.

title: G04: backbone children and extension order must be loaded and written by G05
body: Backbone entries are child nodes keyed <parent>#<element>[index], and each child is a node in the fragment. from_graph walks the children, so a reader that loads only the root and its relationships gets NotFound (same trap as L59). Write each child with its labels, and keep the child props. Extensions are ext_<shortName> props on the root or child node, and a resource with several extensions also stores extensionOrder (a list of short names). Write and load it, or the rebuilt extension list is refused. A reference target that contains # is refused now (# separates child keys). Single and list backbone values differ: a list entry carries order, a single object does not. See DEC-052 items 2, 3 and 10. Found by G04.

title: Neo4j keeps a datetime's fixed offset: L58 was wrong about the offset
body: Probe on the harness Neo4j (G05): a datetime written with +01:00 reads back with a +01:00 fixed offset; a value written in UTC reads back as UTC. Only the text +00:00 comes back as Z, so a zero offset cannot be told apart from Z. L58 said Neo4j does not keep the offset; that holds only when the value was converted to UTC before the write. Do: write the offset-aware value; store a FHIR datetime as a Neo4j datetime only if formatting it again gives the same text (G05 refuses +00:00, .000 and partial dates). Affects G05, I03, P06, G14.

title: A copy of a node must not keep the live labels, or type queries return history
body: G05 writes each version of a resource as a copy of its nodes. If the copy keeps the live labels (HealthcareService_AvailableTime, Organization), every query that matches a label also matches old versions and counts them twice. Give copies their own labels (ResourceVersion, ResourceVersionPart) and let the reader set the root type. Test: count_nodes on the live label after an update (test_removing_one_of_two_available_times). Affects every repository that keeps history (P01 onward, G13).

title: Versioned writes: take the root write lock before reading the version
body: Optimistic versioning is safe only if the version is read after a write lock on the root node. G05 does a write (MERGE ... SET lockStamp) on the root first, then reads versionId. Two writers racing on one version then leave exactly one winner (test_two_writers_racing_on_one_version_let_exactly_one_win). A read before the lock lets both writers see version 1 and both write version 2. Do the same in every repository that checks If-Match. Affects G05 and P01 onward.

title: A subscribe written as an async generator registers on first read, so early publishes are lost
body: An async def generator (or yield-based iterator) runs no code until the first __anext__, so a subscriber that calls subscribe() and publishes before reading misses the message. title: [build-P10] A single-use write must lock before it reads: MATCH ... WHERE ... SET races in Neo4j
body: A query shaped MATCH (t) WHERE t.usedAt IS NULL SET t.usedAt = $at RETURN count(t) is NOT atomic: concurrent callers read the property before any write lock is held, so all of them win (measured on the harness: 8 of 8, then 16 of 16). Setting a property that does not exist to null is a no-op and takes no lock either. The fix that passed 5 rounds of 16 callers, three runs in a row: MATCH the node, SET a property that always exists to its own value (takes the lock), then WITH t WHERE t.usedAt IS NULL SET t.usedAt = $at RETURN count(t). Any first-writer-wins or single-use write (P02 booking claims, P13 approvals, L01 and U25 link burns, P15 idempotency keys) needs a concurrency test with 16 callers, not a sequential one. Test: tests/integration/graph_store/test_link_token_repository.py::test_concurrent_mark_used_lets_exactly_one_caller_win. Query: backend/src/diucs/adapters/outbound/graph_store/link_token_repository.py (Q-LINK-MARK-USED). Decision: DEC-060 item 4.

title: [build-P10] Neo4j stores no null property: a missing key is null, and tests must not expect the key
body: Setting a property to null (or passing None in a CREATE map) stores nothing, so the node has no key. Readers must treat a missing key as None (props.get), and a test that lists a node's properties must leave out the keys that are null for that record. Found in P10: an unused LinkToken has no usedAt key. Affects every repository that stores optional fields (P01 onward). Decision: DEC-060 item 3.

title: Local relationships (no fhirPath) break ResourceStore.get; the loader must skip them
body: A relationship the mapper did not write (for example CHANNEL or COVERED_BY on a PractitionerRole) has no fhirPath property. ResourceStore._load reads every outgoing relationship of the root, and from_graph groups them by fhirPath, so get raised KeyError. P03 (DEC-064 item 7) makes _load skip any relationship without fhirPath; the mapper-written ones always carry it. Every put clears the root's outgoing relationships, so a local relationship must be written again after each put, in the same transaction. Test the cover removal path with a save that drops the cover. Affects P13, P16, P17, P20, P21 (any task with local relationships on a FHIR root).

title: A Neo4j test fixture that seeds data must depend on clean_graph, or the wipe runs after the seed
body: clean_graph is appended to the item closure, so a fixture requested by a test runs before it. A seed fixture then runs before the wipe and its data vanishes: the test fails with a 'not found' that looks like a code bug. Fix: declare clean_graph as a parameter of the seeding fixture (async fixture with loop_scope session), or seed inside the test body. Found by P16: the practitioner seed was wiped before the test ran. Affects every Neo4j integration test with a seeding fixture.

title: A PIN attempt or single-use read must take the write lock first and run in a write transaction
body: Read-judge-save on a counter (PIN failures, link burns, first-writer-wins claims) is racy unless the read takes the write lock: without it, 16 concurrent wrong PINs were all answered wrong (measured). Fix: the query SETs a property that always exists to its own value before it reads (Q-CRED-GET, lesson L73). Such a query is a write, so a test that reads it with read_tx fails with 'Writing in read access mode not allowed': read it with write_tx. The use case must read, judge and save in one unit of work. Decision: DEC-072. Test: test_sixteen_concurrent_wrong_pins_lock_the_device_at_five_failures.

title: A guard whose test is first committed with the guard was never red
body: P16 added four tests in the green commit (9240563), not the red one: a 16-caller PIN race, the naive-time refusal for registration, the naive-time refusal for code issue, and a two-practitioner device race. Each guard was written with its test and never seen failing first, so the test-first rule (delivery-standard item 2) is broken. Do: commit the test for any guard as red before the guard exists, and paste the failing line into the evidence. A mutation run on a guard does not replace the red run. Affects every task that adds a guard beyond its prompt.

title: Verifier worktree: a branch held by the builder's worktree must be checked out detached
body: git worktree add <path> <branch> fails with 'already used by worktree' when the builder has the branch checked out. Use git worktree add --detach <path> <branch>, which checks out the same commit without touching the branch. Do not edit the builder's branch; remove your worktree after recording the verdict.

title: MERGE on a node with no uniqueness constraint races: two first writes create two nodes
body: Neo4j Community has no composite uniqueness, so MERGE (x:Label {a, b}) run by two racing transactions can create two nodes. P16 found it on ProtectedContact (roleId, kind) and it also applies to Credential (practitioner, deviceId) in Q-CRED-SET. Do: add a unique constraint where the key is a single property (Device.id), or take a write lock on a parent node first (the lesson L73 SET trick), then MERGE, and state the residual in a decision if you accept it. Test with 16 racing callers, not one sequential call (lesson L73, L77). Affects P13, P15, P10, U25, U32, P17.

title: L90 update: measure a racing MERGE before deciding; a unique key fixes ProtectedContact
body: Measured by P16 round 2 with sixteen racers. ProtectedContact: sixteen racing first puts for one role made sixteen nodes. It now has a unique key (roleId|kind, migration 0025), and a losing racer gets Conflict and stores nothing. Credential: sixteen racing set_pin calls for one practitioner and device left one node in three runs out of three, because the MERGE creates a relationship from the practitioner node and the engine serialises on that node. No code change; the regression test stays (DEC-073 item 3). Do: for a MERGE on a keyed node, run sixteen racers before you decide. If duplicates appear and a single property can be unique, use a unique constraint; otherwise lock the anchor node first. Same-practitioner racing registrations are a no-op (DEC-073 item 2). Affects P13, P14, P17, P20, U25, U32, U37.

body: P16 round 2: removing the ProtectedContact unique constraint (migration 0025, replaced by a plain index) made test_racing_first_puts_for_one_role_leave_one_protected_contact fail when run alone (16 == 1, 5 of 5) but pass when the file ran in full (9 passed). title: Duplicate Credential nodes defeat the PIN lockout: get reads one row, save_state refuses
body: A second Credential for one practitioner and deviceId is not caught by any constraint (only Device.id is unique). get() takes rows[0] in unspecified order, so a verification can check one of two PIN hashes; save_state then raises NotFound, so the failure count never advances and the 5-try lock cannot engage. Racing set_pin did not reproduce in 1,920 racers (P16 DEC-073 item 3), but absence in test runs is not proof. Do: give Credential a single-property unique key (practitioner id and deviceId joined), as ProtectedContact did in migration 0025, and make get fail closed when more than one row matches. Affects P16, U25, U32, I13.

title: L92 update: a race test's timing is not a guard; use a held transaction to force the interleaving
body: P16 round 3: the timing race (16 racers) failed alone without the unique key but passed in the full file, so it guarded nothing reliably. Do: to test that a unique key holds under a race, hold the first write uncommitted in one session, run the second write as a task, wait until the task is done or one second passes, then commit the first. Without the key the second write creates a second node; with it the second waits and is then refused or updates the committed node. Assert the node count, not the outcome, because the second write may update. Also: a PIN credential's device id is unique in the graph (migration 0026), and reads that find two rows fail closed (DEC-074). Affects P13, P14, P17, P20, U25, U32, U37.

title: Rebasing a long task branch replays every commit: decisions.md conflicts recur at each commit
body: P16 had 13 commits on top of main; rebase stopped on decisions.md at the first commit and again at later ones, because each appends to the same end of file. Resolving by keeping both sides (strip the markers) worked, but takes one step per commit. Do: keep decisions.md entries in a single append at the end of the task, or rebase early, before many commits touch the file. Check afterwards that no DEC number appears twice (grep '^## DEC-' | uniq -d). Affects every builder with a long branch.

body: P12's suites run against InMemoryCache and ManualEventBus, which already pass their own unit tests, so the green run passes at once. The red commit therefore holds the DEC-010 stub factory. To show the guards bite, mutate the fake (subscribe as a generator, stale release freeing the lock, cancel doing nothing, naive times accepted) and confirm a contract test fails for each. P12 caught all 14 mutants. Do the same for I01 (Redis) and I02 (Service Bus emulator). Harness receive: a queue returns due messages, a topic returns messages published since the harness was made. Real factories must clean up in close().

title: pytest -m integration on a suite with no integration tests exits 5, not 0
body: With no test marked integration, pytest -m integration tests/contract collects nothing and exits 5 (no tests collected). The P12 prompt asks that it 'does not error'. A CI step that treats exit 5 as failure will fail until I01 adds the first integration factory. Either accept exit 5 in that step or add the marked param in I01. Found by P12.

title: A link with no fhirPath needs LOCAL_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES, and a service save clears its links
body: The G05 loader skips a relationship with no fhirPath only if its type is in LOCAL_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES (resource_store.py; DEC-065 item 5). Any other local link makes ResourceStore.get raise KeyError 'fhirPath' for the whole resource. P04 added CURRENT_CRITERIA (DEC-076 item 2, red test test_a_service_with_a_current_version_still_reads_and_saves). Add your link type there, with a test. Also: a store put on a resource clears its outgoing relationships (DEC-053 item 6), so a link written from a service is gone after the next ServiceRepository.save. Read such a link back by status, or write it again after every service save. This second point is open: nothing re-points CURRENT_CRITERIA after a service save yet (DEC-076 item 3).

title: Racing writers to one parent: lock the parent first, then check, then write
body: Neo4j Community has no composite uniqueness, so 'one current version per service' and 'one version number per service' cannot be a constraint (lesson L90). P04 takes the service's write lock first (SET s.id = s.id, lesson L73) in every add and save, then runs the checks, then writes. Two held-transaction tests prove it: the second writer must still be waiting after one second, and is then refused (lesson L94). Removing the lock makes both fail (DEC-076 items 4 and 11). Use the same pattern for any single-current or unique-per-parent rule: registrations (P13), flags (P14), criteria approvals (U30).

title: The mapper refuses an empty list: leave empty values out of the FHIR form
body: _map_list raises UnsupportedElement for [] (mapper.py), so a put with an empty list (no districts, no needs, no members) fails. P04 leaves the element out and the rebuild returns the empty set (DEC-076 item 7, lesson L74). A repository that builds lists from possibly empty sets must do the same before its put.

title: A racing test that accepts Conflict as an outcome cannot catch a removed lock
body: P13 scope-list save: the 16-racer test accepted None or Conflict for every racer, so removing the write lock left all 38 tests green. A guard whose job is to let a second writer succeed must assert success for every racer, and its held-transaction test must assert the second writer ends with success, not only that it waits. Run the mutation over the whole test file (lesson L92). Tests: test_scope_list_repository.py::test_sixteen_racing_saves_for_a_new_service_all_succeed_and_leave_one_service and ::test_a_save_for_a_service_that_a_held_save_is_creating_waits_and_succeeds. Decision DEC-082 item 5.

title: A MERGE on an existing relationship already serialises under a held write; only a first create discriminates
body: P13: a held-transaction test in which the second save MERGEs an ENTRY that the held transaction already created still passed with the parent-node lock removed. Neo4j locks both nodes of the pattern, so the second writer waits and then matches. The lock is observable only when the second writer would create the node or relationship for the first time, where the uniqueness constraint refuses it. For every keyed single-writer rule, test the first-create case. Discriminating test: test_a_save_for_a_service_that_a_held_save_is_creating_waits_and_succeeds. Not discriminating: test_a_second_save_for_a_service_waits_for_a_held_save_and_leaves_one_entry.

title: A minimal HealthcareService from the scope list has no profile, so ServiceRepository.get refuses it
body: P13 writes the service of a scope entry before the service registers: HealthcareService with id, active false, name and category, and no profile extensions. P01 profile_from_fhir requires the profile extensions (usualRangeMin and the others) and raises ValidationFailed for such a service. Read it through the scope list (get_entry, entries), or wait until registration writes the full profile. Do not call ServiceRepository.get for a service that has an entry but no profile. Decision DEC-082 item 4.

title: The registration draft is JSON in the prompt, which DEC-001 forbids: store it as typed rows
body: The P13 prompt keeps the wizard draft as an ext_draftJson extension. DEC-001 refuses JSON strings on nodes. P13 stores each step and field as a RegistrationDraftField node joined to the Task by DRAFT_OF, with typed values (DEC-080). U26 and U27 should read and write Registration.draft through draft_to_rows and draft_from_rows, not a JSON extension. The draft is replaced as a whole on save, after the store's write lock.

title: QueryBoard reads confirmations per service: BookingRepository has no batch confirmed_since
body: BookingRepository.confirmed_since takes one service id, so the board calls it once for each service that has a latest report (U08, DEC-085 item 1). The rule 'one query per repository call across all services' cannot hold for confirmations without a new P02 port method. Do: if you need confirmations for many services, add a batch form in a P02 follow-up (for example confirmed_since_for_services returning dict[str, list[datetime]]) before you rely on the board at scale. Pending counts are already batched (open_for_services). Affects U09 (board cache), R05 ($board) and any caller that lists many services.

title: Board sample: a confirmation after the clock is not a fact; read the board later
body: The U08 prompt reads the board at Friday 14:12 but adds a booking confirmed at 14:19. A confirmation after the clock cannot be stored as a past fact for that read. U08 tests it by reading the confirmed step at 14:25 (13:25 UTC) and asserting the result, not the time (DEC-085 item 3). Do the same in any test that mixes a clock with sample times from the artboards. The Main artboard samples (ui-screens.md) use times up to 16:00, so check each one against the clock before you write it as a fact. Note also: a sync test in a module with pytestmark asyncio emits a warning, so make it async.

title: Catch unhandled API errors in an outer middleware: Starlette's 500 handler lets the server log the message
body: Starlette's exception handler for Exception responds with 500 and then re-raises, so uvicorn logs the message and the traceback. A FHIR error can carry a postcode, so the message leaks into the server log. R01 uses an outer ASGI middleware (UnhandledErrorMiddleware in adapters/inbound/fhir_rest/errors.py) that logs the exception class name only and sends the OperationOutcome itself. Do the same in any new inbound adapter. Decision: DEC-085 item 4. Test: tests/integration/adapters/inbound/fhir_rest/test_app.py::test_an_unexpected_error_is_logged_without_its_message_or_trace.

title: Redis SUBSCRIBE is live only when the server confirms it: publish waits for that confirmation
body: redis-py sends SUBSCRIBE and reads the server reply later, so a PUBLISH sent right after subscribe() can be lost. The I01 adapter starts SUBSCRIBE in a task, waits for the server subscribe reply, and RedisCache.publish waits for every subscription that cache made before it sends. This holds inside one process only. A publish from another process can still be missed in the round trip after subscribe(). Do: a live-update consumer must refetch its data on connect and after any reconnect, and must not assume a publish from another worker reaches it right after subscribe(). Tests: tests/contract/test_cache_contract.py (publish-between-subscribe-and-read case, redis id); mutant with the barrier removed fails 6 or 7 cases.

title: A Redis fencing counter is only as durable as its Redis: data loss restarts tokens at 1
body: acquire_lock takes its token from INCR on diucs:fence:<name>, which never expires (DEC-058 item 2). The compose Redis has no volume, and a managed Redis can lose data or restart, after which the counter starts again and a new holder can receive a token an old holder already used. Redis alone cannot keep tokens increasing across that event. Do: a writer guarded by a fencing token must also compare the token with the highest token it has already committed in Neo4j, which is a fact of record, before it writes. The outbox relay lock (I03) must do this. Do not rely on Redis for this guarantee. Recorded in DEC-089 item 4.

title: A close test must wait until the reader is blocked, or it tests the closed path instead of the wake-up
body: A reader started with ensure_future and then closed at once takes the closed-subscription branch before it waits on the queue, so a test named close wakes a waiting reader passes even with the wake-up removed (mutant survived in I01). Do: await the subscription opened task, start the reader, await asyncio.sleep(0) so it blocks on the empty queue, then close. Then confirm the test fails with the wake-up line removed. Test: tests/unit/adapters/outbound/cache_redis/test_redis_cache.py::test_a_closed_subscription_ends_a_reader_that_is_waiting.

title: redis-py pubsub: one reader per connection, and close by UNSUBSCRIBE plus its reply
body: get_message with timeout None blocks, and two tasks reading one PubSub take each other replies. The I01 adapter gives each subscription one reader task that ends on the unsubscribe reply, and closes the connection only after that reply, so PUBSUB NUMSUB is 0 when aclose returns. Closing the connection without UNSUBSCRIBE can leave NUMSUB at 1 for a moment, which is a race, not a pass. Test: tests/integration/adapters/outbound/cache_redis/test_redis_cache.py::test_closing_a_subscription_unsubscribes_it.

title: The Redis cache suite is the first integration factory: -m integration tests/contract now exits 0
body: With the redis factory marked integration, pytest -m integration tests/contract collects 23 cache cases and exits 0 (DEC-077 item 4). The Redis factories share the compose Redis and flush only diucs:* keys before and after each case, so they need no per-session container. Other sessions running the cache suite at the same time share the diucs: keyspace. Use the same factory shape for the Service Bus emulator (I02).

title: A racing MERGE on a unique key waits, then matches: it returns not-new, not Conflict
body: P15 measured two concurrent MERGE on a keyed node with a unique constraint. The second MERGE waits for the held first write; after the first commits it matches the committed node and returns not-new. It raises ConstraintError only when a CREATE meets the key. Expect a racing test to see False for the waiter, and write the expectation from the measured behaviour. A held-transaction test must assert the count of nodes, which is 1 with the constraint and 2 without it. Affects P13, P14, P17, U25, U30, U32.

title: Compare instants with astimezone(UTC) before asserting equality across zones
body: Python compares two aware datetimes in different zones by instant only when neither is ambiguous. On 2026-10-25 a London 01:55 is ambiguous (PEP 495, fold 0 is BST): comparing it with a UTC value of the same instant can be False. In a test, convert the expected value with astimezone(UTC) first, then compare. Found in P15 (test_a_london_datetime_comes_back_as_the_same_instant_in_utc). Affects any test that round-trips a London time.

title: The Cache port subscribe is async now: await it, and it returns only once the server confirms
body: Changed by I01 (DEC-092). Callers must write subscription = await cache.subscribe(channel). subscribe returns only after the server has the subscription, so a publish sent right after it is delivered. The memory fake matches. Publish is no longer gated in-process. The owner must add this signature change to contracts.md Additions. Lesson L117 (subscribe confirmation) is superseded by this rule. Affects I05, U08, R06, I03.

title: A fencing token that must grow across a Redis loss cannot start at 1: the first token of a lock name is no longer 1
body: DEC-091 issues max(INCR, host clock in microseconds). A fresh counter and a lost counter look the same to Redis, so a lock name's first token is a large number, not 1. Two contract cases assert 1 and fail on the Redis adapter until the owner rules (DEC-091 item 4). Do not weaken those cases. Consumers must compare tokens only with the last token recorded in Neo4j, never assume the first token is 1. Affects I03, I05.

title: L90 correction: Community Neo4j does refuse a duplicate composite unique key
body: L90 said Neo4j Community lacks composite uniqueness. A verifier probe on Neo4j 5.26.32 Community (P15, round 1) found a composite unique constraint refuses a duplicate. L90's advice still holds (a single-property unique key is the safest, and a MERGE on a keyed node races without one), but the claim that composite keys are unavailable is wrong. Do not cite L90 for that. Affects P15 (DEC-090 items 5 and 10), and any earlier decision that repeats the claim: P16 DEC-071 item 1, DEC-073, DEC-074, P04, P13, P14.

title: Service Bus emulator: cancel of a non-pending number is an error; session receives need a longer open window
body: Emulator 2.0.1 findings (I02). (1) cancel_scheduled_messages on a sequence number that is unknown, already delivered, or held by another queue raises ServiceBusError whose text is 'The scheduled message with SequenceNumber = N is already being cancelled'. Cancel of a pending message succeeds. The port says cancel of an unknown or delivered number does nothing, so the contract and the emulator disagree; do not weaken the case, record a DEC first. (2) Receiving from a session-enabled subscription with ServiceBusSessionFilter.NEXT_AVAILABLE and a short max_wait_time (0.3 s) raises OperationTimeoutError on opening the link when nothing is waiting; use a longer open window and treat that timeout as no message. (3) A contract run that drains and receives topic messages took over 280 s for 8 cases, so run the servicebus factory with a timeout and expect the topic cases to be slow. Affects I02, I03, I05.

title: A booking Task has no Task.code, so the reporter projection covers every Task (fail closed); fhir.resources 8.3 names

A projection that changes a resource gets meta.security REDACTED; one that changes nothing gets no label. In fhir.resources 8.3 use resource.get_resource_type() (there is no resource_type attribute) and the 'for' element is the attribute for_fhir (alias 'for' in JSON). title: SmsSender consumers: a refused send has provider id '' and a retry after a timeout can send twice
body: DEC-101 (I06). (1) A Twilio refusal (21211, 21614, 21610) returns SendReceipt('', False): Twilio issues no sid, so the consumer must store no provider id (not the empty string) and must not look it up. (2) TransientSendError on a timeout does not prove the text was not sent. The consumer retries with the same message id, and a duplicate text is possible; there is no Twilio idempotency key on this path. (3) SendFailedError (any other answer) is not retried: record it as failed for staff, do not loop. Tasks: I10 (consumer of messages.outbound), I07 (status callback).

title: A self-SET of a changing property writes back a stale value: lock with a fresh stamp, then read
body: Found by R03. SET t.versionId = t.versionId takes the write lock, but the value it writes is the one read before the lock was granted. A writer that held the node and committed version 4 was overwritten with 3 when the waiting statement ran: the PUT returned 200 instead of 412 on the harness Neo4j. Do: SET a separate lockStamp to a fresh value in one statement, then read the version in a second statement, as the G05 Q-RES-LOCK query does. The self-SET trick of lesson L73 is for properties that never change, such as an id. Test: backend/tests/integration/adapters/inbound/fhir_rest/test_concurrency.py::test_a_put_waits_for_a_held_write_then_sees_the_new_version_and_is_refused (a held uncommitted write; the request must wait, then see the committed version).

title: Test harness containers must be removed with -v: docker rm -f alone leaks two anonymous volumes per run
body: The neo4j image declares anonymous VOLUMEs for /data and /logs. docker rm -f <name> leaves them, and the harness did this until F10-fix (70 volumes, 18 GB in about an hour; the disk filled). Any container a test starts must be removed with docker rm -f -v (DEC-128), or given a named volume you remove yourself. Clean existing leaks with docker volume prune -f, which only removes volumes no container references. Check with: docker volume ls -qf dangling=true | wc -l before and after a run.
